rationale: The workflow triggers on pull_request with a single build job. Multiple pushes to the same PR create superseded runs that waste CI resources. Adding concurrency with cancel-in-progress cancels stale runs for the same workflow and ref (PR branch), preserving the latest check. This matches pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (cancel superseded runs) which reports 4.1% paid VM time reduction. Preconditions are met: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, and a newer revision supersedes older checks. No contraindications apply (not release/deployment work; distinct branches are isolated by github.ref). The gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v5 action already caches Gradle dependencies, so adding an explicit cache step (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) would be redundant per its contraindication 'An equivalent cache already exists'. No representative run history exists to set a custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT).
